chunks: One of our companions wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) complaining to him about blood and paleness, saying, 'When I get cupping done, the paleness increases, and when I delay the cupping, the blood harms me. So what is your view regarding that?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Get cupping done and eat upon the effects of the cupping, fresh grilled fish.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I re-iterated the same question to him, so he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'Get cupping done and eat upon the effects of the cupping, fresh grilled fish with water and salt.' He (the narrator) said, 'So I acted upon that, so I was in good health and it became my regular intake.'

key_terms.صَفْرَاء: Paleness (a symptom of blood deficiency or weakness)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam advise for someone suffering from side effects of cupping?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical medical solution to the dilemma of cupping-induced weakness by prescribing fresh fish, highlighting the Shia tradition of integrating spiritual guidance with empirical health practices. The specific recommendation to consume grilled fish with water and salt immediately after cupping underscores the concept of *tadafu* (complementary pairing) in traditional medicine, where the nutrient-dense fish counteracts the depletion caused by bloodletting, ensuring the patient remains in a state of well-being.

en.hubeali:
‘One of our companions wrote to Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> complaining to him<sup>asws</sup> about blood and paleness saying, ‘When I get cupping done, it leads to paleness, and when I delay the cupping, so what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding that?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Get cupping done and eat upon the effects of cupping, fresh grilled fish’. 
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I re-iterated the same question to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Get cupping done, and eat upon the effects of the cupping, fresh grilled fish with water and salt. He (the narrator) said, ‘So I worked upon that, so I was upon good health and it became my (regular) intake’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated the following:

“Certain persons of our people once wrote to abu Muhammad, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, complaining about blood and yellowness, saying, ‘If I apply cupping, yellowness stirs up, when I delay it blood harms me, so what would you advise me in such case?’ He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote, ‘Apply cupping and after cupping eat fresh fish as kabab.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I repeated exactly the same question to him (the Imam). He (the Imam) wrote, ‘Apply cupping and after cupping eat fresh fish as kabab with water and salt.’ He (the narrator) has said, ‘I followed the instruction and I lived in good health and it became my food.’”
